text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A British team contracted by the Kenya Ports Authority to run the container terminal fails to improve cargo handling.
- The University of Nairobi will re-open on Monday after its closure last month during protests by students mourning the death of their colleague Solomon Muruli.
- Leaders from the Eastern districts of Samburu, Marsabit and Isiolo meet to discuss rising tension along the borders.
-The former wife of a cabinet minister involved in a child lesbian syndicate will be transferred overseas by her employee.
- At least 25 Somali refugees are seriously injured in a clash at the closed Swaleh Nguru refugee camp in Mombasa.
- The government has banned importation of dairy products, excluding white or dried infant food, for the next nine months.
- German ambassador to Kenya urges for the introduction of a code of conduct to deter political leaders from using ethnicity to pit communities against each other.
- Starehe Boys Centre is in a financial crisis after major sponsors Save the Children Fund withdrew their sponsorship. ($1=55 Kenyan shillings)
